name: Bwela
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Twilingiyima, Chrysogone 1984, Elements de description du Doko (grammar, Glottolog MED 687569); also Hulstaert 1961, Sur le parler Doko (Aequatoria); neither loadable

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza, Jean-Pierre. 2014. L'idéophone en Ebwela, langue bantoue du nord-ouest de la RD Congo. Studies in African Linguistics 43(1&2): 1-24. doi:10.32473/sal.v43i1.107267
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 'Tons' (p.10): Ebwela has two level tones H/L combining into rising/falling contours, vowel is the tone-bearing unit, tonal minimal pair given; the word 'accent'/'stress' never occurs in the article.

sources.citation: WALS Online, lect 'Bwele' (wals code dok), citing Twilingiyimana 1984
sources.note: Only six word-order values (81A-95A); no tone/stress/rhythm features coded.

sources.citation: Hulstaert, Gustaaf. 1961. Sur le parler Dɔkɔ. Aequatoria 24(4): 121-135.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Short 'Phonologie' (7 vowels, implosives) and a 'Tonologie' section (pp.127-130: prefixes H, falling tone on prefix before monosyllabic stems, Doko falling tone corresponding to Mongo L first stem syllable, etc.). Purely tonal treatment; no mention of stress/accent. Informant from Monzelenge checked by two Bwela pupils from Ndeke (Ngombe-Doko).

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles / Universiteit Gent. xvi+466 pp. (ULB-digitised copy on DI-fusion)
sources.note: Ch.1 sec.1.3 'La tonologie' (pp.62-67): all ten languages incl. Ebwela have two basic tones H/L plus rising/falling contours, vowel = tone-bearing mora; Ebwela surface tone schemes listed. p.45: in Ebwela some stem-internal H vowels (often the medial syllable of trisyllables, or the vowel before an NC cluster) are pronounced long with a contour tone 'sans que cette longueur soit distinctive'. No statement on stress/accent anywhere ('accent' only as 'accent aigu/grave' diacritics).

sources.citation: Rood, N. 1962. Lidoko et Mowea. Aequatoria 25: 125-139.
sources.note: Word-by-word comparison of Hulstaert's Doko data with Mowea (Lingombe C41); remarks on vowels and tones only ('les voyelles et les tons sont les éléments les plus significatifs'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du Nord-Ouest du Congo belge. Institut Royal Colonial Belge, Bulletin des Séances 22(4): 900-919.
sources.note: Sec. D 'Tonologie Dókó' (pp.909-913): 'tons doubles courts' (short contour tones felt as a third simple tone), fixed word tonology, H noun prefixes, historical tone shift; nothing on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Twilingiyimana, Chrysogone. 1984. Eléments de description du doko. Mémoire de licence spéciale en linguistique africaine, Université Libre de Bruxelles (copy at MRAC Tervuren linguistics library). xii+109 pp.
